$$A=\dfrac{b-a}{2n}\left\{f(a)+f(b)+2\left[f(x_1)+f(x_2)+f(x_3)\right]\right\}$$ $$=\dfrac{5-(-5)}{2\times4}\left\{0+0+2\left[\sqrt{18.75}+5+\sqrt{18.75}\right]\right\}=34.15063509$$ $$=34.151\ \text{units}^2\ (3\text{ d.p.})$$

solutions.latex:
Points of intersection: $x^3-x^2-kx+2=-x^2+2$, so $x^3-kx=0$, $x(x^2-k)=0$, $x=0$ or $x=\pm\sqrt k$.

For A: $\left(x^3-x^2-kx+2\right)-\left(-x^2+2\right)=x^3-kx$

$$A=\int_{-\sqrt k}^{0}\left(x^3-kx\right)dx=\left[\dfrac{x^4}{4}-\dfrac{kx^2}{2}\right]_{-\sqrt k}^{0}=0-\left(\dfrac{k^2}{4}-\dfrac{k^2}{2}\right)=\dfrac{k^2}{4}$$

For B: $\left(-x^2+2\right)-\left(x^3-x^2-kx+2\right)=-x^3+kx$

$$B=\int_0^{\sqrt k}\left(-x^3+kx\right)dx=\left[-\dfrac{x^4}{4}+\dfrac{kx^2}{2}\right]_0^{\sqrt k}=-\dfrac{k^2}{4}+\dfrac{k^2}{2}=\dfrac{k^2}{4}$$

$\therefore A=B$

Note: if an indefinite integral is used, $-1$ (the constant $C$ needs to cancel); if an incorrect intersection is found then CFE.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: intersections $x=0,\pm\sqrt k$; 1: area A $=\frac{k^2}{4}$; 1: area B $=\frac{k^2}{4}$; 1: conclusion $A=B$

solutions.latex:
$D$ is a minimum when $D^2$ is. Find the minimum stationary point of $D^2$.

$\dfrac{d(D^2)}{dt}=78t-60$

Stationary point when $\dfrac{d(D^2)}{dt}=0$: $78t-60=0$, $t=\dfrac{60}{78}=\dfrac{10}{13}$.

Test: $t=0.7,\ \frac{10}{13},\ 0.8$ gives $\dfrac{d(D^2)}{dt}=-5.4,\ 0,\ 2.4$, so a minimum stationary point.

$D^2=39\left(\tfrac{10}{13}\right)^2-60\left(\tfrac{10}{13}\right)+400=371.597633\ldots$

$D=19.28$ km (2 d.p.)

Note: most students forgot to test to show a minimum, OR use the property of the original function (concave up parabola).
